newsitem.title: UK: UK consumer body wants Energy bid reviewed.
newsitem.headline: UK consumer body wants Energy bid reviewed.

text.p: A British consumer watchdog body called on the government on Friday to refer U.S. group PacifiCorp's bid for The Energy Group to competition authorities on public interest grounds.

The National Consumer Council (NCC) said in a statement it had pressed Stephen Littlechild, the head of electricity industry regulator Offer, to recommend a referral of the bid to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC).
PacifiCorp's 3.7 billion pound bid for Britain's biggest electricity distributor is the first in the sector since the centre-left Labour government swept to power in a landslide victory on May 1.

Previous bids for regional electricity companies (Recs), privatised by the previous Conservative government in 1990, were largely waved through under its administration, leaving Southern Electric alone of the original 12 still independent.
Rec Eastern Electricity was taken over by Hanson, which then demerged it with The Energy Group earlier this year.
The Energy Group, which agreed to the bid, has said it does not see any regulatory hurdles.

But analysts have said the new government could take a harder line and point to a referral to the MMC by trade secretary Margaret Beckett of National Express bids for two rail franchises at the end of May, against the advice of the Office of Fair Trading (OFT).
Littlechild launched a study of PacifiCorp's bid on June 16, inviting comments by June 23.
"Takeovers...have delivered nothing in the way of price cuts to consumers. Shareholders, on the other hand, have benefited handsomely," NCC director Ruth Evans said in a statement.

Labour fiercely criticised utilities for hefty dividend payouts, weighty executive wage packets and spiralling takeovers and has vowed to impose a tax on their "excess profits" in its first budget on July 2.

Evans said takeovers also made it "much harder to scrutinise and to make comparisons now that key financial facts and figures...are entangled with information on the bigger, diversified parent companies."
The NCC said it was sending copies of its letter to John Bridgman, head of the OFT, hoping that he would advise Beckett that the bid should be reviewed by the MMC.

Concerns that the bid might not overcome regulatory hurdles have kept the Energy Group's share price at a discount to the bid level of 690 pence plus a 5.5 pence dividend. In late trading, the stock was down one penny at 641-1/2p.
